diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $u$ is the exact solution of \eqref{eqn:fZK} satisfying $u \in C^1([0,T]; H^r_{\text{per}}(\Omega))$ with $r \geq \alpha + 1$

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and contributions list say that data in H^r give the rate N^{-r}. The theorem instead assumes the exact solution is C^1 in time with values in H^r. Since u_t = ∂_{x1}(-Δ)^{α/2}u - u u_{x1} loses 1+α derivatives, this needs u in C([0,T];H^{r+1+α}), hence u_0 in H^{r+1+α}. Data in H^r alone do not satisfy the hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: The method achieves spectral convergence of order $\mathcal{O}(N^{-r})$ for initial data in $H^r_{\mathrm{per}}$ with $r \geq \alpha+1$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract and contribution bullets in terms of the theorem's hypothesis (solution in C^1([0,T];H^r), which requires u_0 in H^{r+1+α}), or prove the estimate under weaker hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised regularity requirement for the rate N^{-r} is understated by 1+α derivatives. The theorem itself is unchanged.
issues.title: Abstract/intro claim O(N^{-r}) for initial data in H^r, but the theorem needs u in C^1([0,T];H^r)
issues.why_classification: The edit is local, but the advertised data regularity changes materially, so the headline convergence claim is weaker than stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows \cite[Lemma 2.4]{dwivedi2024numerical} and adapts it to the two-dimensional setting.

issues.failure_explanation: The one-sided pointwise inequality is false for the spectrally defined operator. For f=1, α=2, C=2 it reads (-Δ)g ≤ 2(-Δ)g, which fails wherever (-Δ)g<0, and a mean-zero g must be negative somewhere. A one-sided inequality also cannot be inserted into an inner product with a sign-changing function. The norm 'consequence' needs absolute values. The proof is only a citation to a 1D paper. The true Kato–Ponce/commutator estimate has remainder terms, which the energy estimate drops.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lemma by a correct Kato–Ponce commutator estimate for [(-Δ)^{(1+α)/2}, u]∂_{x1}u, with the Fourier-defined fractional Laplacian on the torus. Then redo the nonlinear estimate, keeping the integration-by-parts structure that is already present.
issues.overall_effect: The key H^{1+α} a priori bound (bd3), and everything built on it (compactness, existence, uniqueness, spectral convergence), rests on an invalid step.
issues.title: Pointwise product estimate is false/unproven and does not justify the nonlinear energy estimate
issues.why_classification: The a priori estimate stays available through a standard commutator lemma and a reworked estimate with the same conclusion, so no global architecture is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The crucial observation is that the existence time $\bar{T}$ depends on $\|u_0\|_{1+\alpha}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Bound (bd3) comes from dD/dt ≤ C D^{3/2}, which only controls the norm up to T̄ = 1/(C√D_0), where the bound is 2‖u_0‖. It is not uniform in time. Restarting from t = T̄ with doubled norm gives a time step half as long, and so on. The steps sum to the blow-up time T_b = 2/(C√D_0) of the comparison ODE, never to an arbitrary T. The conserved quantities control only H^{α/2}, not H^{1+α}, so no global bound is available.

failure_location.quote: Since the semi-discrete approximation is bounded on the $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}$-norm uniformly in time \eqref{bd3}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Theorem thm:exisuq and the convergence claims as local-in-time on [0,T*] with T* depending on ‖u_0‖_{1+α}. Alternatively, assume the exact solution exists on [0,T] with uniform bounds and bootstrap the semi-discrete H^{1+α} bound.
issues.overall_effect: Existence and uniqueness 'for all T ≥ 0' and convergence of u_N on arbitrary [0,T] are unsupported. The a priori bound used in the error analysis for t up to T is available only on [0,T̄].
issues.title: Continuation to arbitrary T uses an H^{1+α} bound that is only local in time
issues.why_classification: The global-in-time existence and convergence claim is the stated theorem. Without new global a priori estimates it must be abandoned for a standard local result.

issues.failure_explanation: For C([0,T̄];L^2), Arzelà–Ascoli needs equicontinuity and, for each t, relative compactness of {u_N(t)} in L^2. L^2 boundedness does not give compactness in infinite dimensions. The needed compactness would come from the uniform H^{1+α} bound (bd3) and Rellich's theorem, which the proof never invokes.

failure_location.quote: Combined with the uniform boundedness in $L^2_{\text{per}}(\Omega)$ from \eqref{bd1}, the Arzelà-Ascoli theorem guaranties the existence of a subsequence

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add that {u_N(t)} is bounded in H^{1+α}, which embeds compactly in L^2 on the torus, so the pointwise relative compactness hypothesis holds.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the existence of the uniformly convergent subsequence is not justified.
issues.title: Arzelà–Ascoli applied with only L^2 boundedness
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence fix with the already available bound (bd3) and the standard compact embedding repairs it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: through a fractional Laplacian of order $\alpha \in [1,2]$

issues.failure_explanation: The a priori estimate, the uniqueness argument and the error proof need ‖∂_{x1}u‖_{L^∞} ≲ ‖u‖_{1+α}. On the 2D torus this requires 1+α>2, i.e. α>1. At α=1, H^2(T^2) does not embed in W^{1,∞}. The error proof bounds ‖∂_{x1}(u-Π̃u)‖_∞ by |·|_2, which is false in 2D for any α because ∂u∈H^1 is not in L^∞. The stated scope α∈[1,2] is therefore not covered.

failure_location.quote: Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Sobolev embedding $H^{1+\alpha}(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^\infty(\Omega)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to α∈(1,2], or assume H^s regularity with s>2 at α=1. Replace the |·|_2 bound by |·|_{1+α}, which is bounded by the projection estimate with l=α+1.
issues.overall_effect: The a priori bound, uniqueness and the error estimate are unproved for α=1, which the paper highlights as the Benjamin–Ono-type case. The 2-seminorm step in the error proof is incorrect as written.
issues.title: H^{1+α} ↪ W^{1,∞} used in 2D, which fails at α=1 (and |·|_2 used for ‖∂u‖_∞)
issues.why_classification: A contained hypothesis change or restriction, plus replacing the Sobolev step, repairs it. The proof architecture is unchanged, but the α=1 endpoint of the advertised range is excluded or needs more regularity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: While the adaptation from the one-dimensional Kawahara setting to our multidimensional fractional ZK equation requires careful handling of the fractional Laplacian and the additional spatial dimension
Let $u \in C^1(\Omega)$ be a smooth function.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound ‖w-Π̃_N w‖_l ≤ C N^{l-r}|w|_r for all r and 0≤l≤α+1 is the core of the 'optimal error' claim. The paper gives no proof and cites a 1D integer-order Kawahara analysis. Here the operator is nonlocal and 2D, the coefficient u is only C^1, and the principal part is skew-adjoint (coercive only in L^2). A direct stability argument gives only N^{1-r}. The optimal rate needs a duality argument whose regularity requirements are not checked.

failure_location.quote: we omit the detailed proofs and refer readers to \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the complete methodology

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified. At minimum, give a full duality-based proof of the projection estimates (and their time-derivative version) for this operator, with explicit regularity assumptions on u. Otherwise weaken the claim to a rate that follows from a direct argument.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal N^{-r} error estimate for the semi-discrete scheme, the main error-analysis claim, has no supporting proof in the paper.
issues.title: Optimal modified-projection estimate asserted without proof for a nonlocal, 2D, variable-coefficient operator
issues.why_classification: The central optimal-rate theorem depends entirely on an unproved result needing a substantial new argument, and the source supports no complete resolution.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where we assume that $r$ is proportional to $N$

issues.failure_explanation: Several steps fail. (i) r! ≤ r^r e^{-r} is false, since r! ~ √(2πr)(r/e)^r. (ii) |w|_r ≤ r!‖w‖ is an unstated analyticity bound that holds only for analytic w with constants depending on the strip. (iii) The constant C in (proj_erro) depends on r. Letting r grow with N requires C uniform in r, which is not shown (and the estimate is only proved for fixed r). The condition l≤min{r,α+1} is also ignored.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the exponential estimate directly. Writing Π̃_N w - Π_N w = ξ, coercivity gives ‖ξ‖ ≲ ‖u‖_∞‖w-Π_N w‖_1, which decays exponentially for analytic w. This avoids the r-dependent constants.
issues.overall_effect: The exponential-convergence statement (proj_erro2), and the abstract's exponential-convergence claim, are unsupported.
issues.title: Exponential projection estimate derived via an invalid Stirling/r∝N argument
issues.why_classification: A short contained argument based on coercivity and Fourier tail decay yields the exponential rate without new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, let $w$ be an analytic function on $\Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses exponential bounds for u - Π̃_N u and ∂_t(Π̃_N u - u) at every t in [0,T]. This needs u(t) analytic with a uniform strip on [0,T]. The paper proves no propagation of analyticity from u_0 for this nonlocal dispersive equation, where the strip may shrink or the solution may leave the class. Only the algebraic time-derivative estimate (time_error) exists, not an exponential one.

failure_location.quote: If, in addition, the initial data \(u_0\) is real-analytic, then there exist positive constants \(C\) and \(\sigma\), independent of \(N\), such that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the hypothesis to 'the solution u and ∂_t u are analytic with a uniform strip on [0,T]' (as the abstract's 'analytic solutions' suggests). Add the exponential bound for ∂_t(Π̃_N u - u), e.g. via the coercivity argument.
issues.overall_effect: The exponential-convergence part of the theorem, as stated for analytic initial data, is unsupported.
issues.title: Analytic-data exponential convergence assumes u(t) analytic with exponentially small ∂_t projection error
issues.why_classification: Restating the hypothesis and adding a contained exponential time-derivative estimate resolves it, with a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with initial data $u_0 \in H_{\mathrm{per}}^{r}(\Omega)$, $r \geq \alpha + 5$, and assume the nonlinear term $\mathcal{N}$ is sufficiently smooth

issues.failure_explanation: The O(Δt^5) remainder involves time derivatives of F(t,V)=e^{-Lt}N(e^{Lt}V) up to order 5 along the solution, and each t-derivative produces a factor of L, of size N^{1+α}. Uniformity in N therefore needs about 5(1+α) derivatives (plus those from N) of the solution in H^r. The stated r≥α+5 does not give this. The claim is simply asserted, yet this N-uniformity is the substance of an integrating-factor error analysis.

failure_location.quote: Under the regularity assumption, the constant in the $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^5)$ term is bounded uniformly in $N$, completing the proof of the local error estimate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the regularity hypothesis to cover the needed time derivatives. Bound the elementary differentials of F along the exact solution in terms of ‖u‖_{H^r}, using that e^{±Lt} is unitary, so the bound is N-independent.
issues.overall_effect: The N-uniform Δt^5 local error bound, and the Δt^4 temporal rate in the fully discrete estimate, are unsupported under the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: Local truncation error constant claimed N-independent without argument; regularity r≥α+5 inadequate
issues.why_classification: It needs a contained derivative-counting argument and a larger regularity assumption, but the Δt^4 conclusion is plausible and the method is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: consider the linearized version of the fZK equation where the nonlinear term is replaced by \(\lambda \partial_{x_1} u\), with \(\lambda \in \mathbb{R}\)
The method achieves optimal convergence rates in both space and time

issues.failure_explanation: Passing from an O(Δt^5) local error to an O(Δt^4) global error, and combining with the spatial error, needs stability (a discrete Lipschitz/Gronwall argument) of the nonlinear IFRK4 map with constants independent of N. The paper gives only a linear von Neumann analysis with constant λ and no error recursion or bound on the numerical solution. Also, the fully discrete bound has C1, C2 'independent of N and Δt' resting on the unproved N-uniform local error. No fully discrete theorem is stated or proved, yet 'optimal convergence rates in both space and time' is claimed.

failure_location.quote: The global error accumulates as $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^4)$ over $\mathcal{O}(1/\Delta t)$ time steps.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a fully discrete convergence theorem. This needs Lipschitz stability of the nonlinear IFRK map on a ball in a suitable norm, uniform-in-N bounds for the numerical solution, and an error recursion. Otherwise restrict the claim to linear stability plus local truncation error.
issues.overall_effect: The error analysis of the fully discrete scheme, advertised in the abstract, is unsupported. Only a linear stability condition and a local error statement are given.
issues.title: Fully discrete error bound C1 N^{-r} + C2 Δt^4 asserted without nonlinear stability or proof
issues.why_classification: A standard but nontrivial contained argument (stability plus Gronwall) is missing, and a weaker comparable claim survives.
